categories.name: AI Control and Agentic Safety
categories.description: Research on overseeing, monitoring, red-teaming and evaluating autonomous LLM agents that may be misaligned or misused, including control protocols, monitors, scheming/sabotage evaluations, multi-agent risks, prompt injection and agent benchmark integrity.

categories.name: Trusted and Untrusted Monitoring Protocols
categories.description: Theory and empirics of AI control protocols built on trusted or untrusted monitors: collusion between monitors and agents, attack selection, monitor transfer and calibration, co-trained monitors, untrusted advice, and statistical limits of safety assurance.

categories.name: Live Agent Misuse and Shutdown Resistance
categories.description: Red-teaming and evaluations of deployed computer-, phone- and robot-use agents for harmful actions, misuse, meltdowns, corrigibility failures, and resistance or sabotage of shutdown.

categories.name: Misalignment in Multi-Agent Organizations
categories.description: Studies of how agent organizations, delegation structures, agent markets, memory and action histories produce or amplify misaligned behavior such as peer-preservation, unsafe continuation, and emergent misaligned communication.

categories.name: Control Evaluation Settings and Environments
categories.description: New control settings and arenas (e.g. LinuxArena, ResearchArena, Control OSWorld) and simulated control evaluations that measure whether monitors catch covert sabotage under realistic deployment conditions.

categories.name: Coding Agent Overreach and Sabotage
categories.description: Evaluations of coding agents taking out-of-scope actions, overclaiming completion, escalating privileges, constructing jailbreaks via IDE workflows, or sabotaging code undetected by human developers.

categories.name: Agent Trace Auditing and Tampering
categories.description: Methods for auditing large sets of agent traces for safety violations and evidence that agents can tamper with their own traces or harnesses, undermining post-hoc oversight.

categories.name: Scheming Detection and Monitor Evasion
categories.description: Black-box and latent monitors for detecting scheming and sabotage, honeypot and in-the-wild scheming detection, production monitors, blocking monitors, and agents learning or choosing to evade monitoring.

categories.name: Multi-Agent Collusion and Covert Coordination
categories.description: Detection, emergence and mitigation of collusion, steganography, coercion, persuasion and self-propagating ideas among interacting LLM agents, plus game-theoretic models of AI cooperation and bargaining.

categories.name: Red-Teaming Agent Monitors
categories.description: Benchmarks and pipelines that stress-test coding-agent monitors and blocking classifiers with evasive attacks, distributed attacks, long contexts, and transcript editing, including red-teams of production monitors and resampling protocols.

categories.name: Sabotage Propensity and Loss-of-Control Evaluations
categories.description: Evaluations and frameworks for whether models scheme, pursue instrumental goals, sabotage safety research or self-improvement, plus self-incrimination training, training-run evaluations, and assessments of loss-of-oversight and loss-of-control risk.

categories.name: Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
categories.description: Indirect prompt injection against agents, its mechanisms (role confusion, reasoning-time decisions), training and architectural defenses, skill-file attacks, and incident reports of rogue agent hacking activity.

categories.name: Evaluation Integrity and Agent Security Threats
categories.description: Threats undermining evaluations and deployment security: rare-action defection, benchmark/verifier hacking and hardening, cheating on cyber tasks, memory and weight backdoors, sandbox fingerprinting, inference verification, and security leaderboards.

categories.name: Control Roadmaps and Distributed Threats
categories.description: Lab control roadmaps, insider-threat detection, diffuse and multi-agent distributed attacks on per-instance monitors, automated red-teaming at scale, and multi-step cyber-attack capability ranges.

categories.name: Autonomous AI R&D Capability Benchmarks
categories.description: Benchmarks measuring agents' ability to automate AI research, build agents, complete long coding tasks or escape sandboxes, and audits of benchmark validity and reward hacking in agent evaluations.

categories.name: Interpretability and Training-Data Effects
categories.description: Research on understanding model internals (features, circuits, parameters, geometry, introspection) and on how training data shapes learned behaviour and generalization, including attribution and data-driven control.

categories.name: Training Data Attribution and Behaviour Discovery
categories.description: Methods that trace post-training or fine-tuning behaviours back to responsible datapoints (influence functions, probe-based attribution), predict or shape out-of-distribution generalization by editing data, or discover and elicit unexpected learned behaviours.

categories.name: Circuits, Parameters, and Mechanistic Estimation
categories.description: Foundational mechanistic interpretability on neurons, sparse circuits, and parameter decomposition, plus ARC-style mechanistic estimation on random MLPs and tiny uninterpreted models; includes debates over whether neurons are already interpretable.

categories.name: Subliminal Learning and Hidden Data Signals
categories.description: Work on traits, backdoors, or capabilities transmitted through semantically unrelated data or weak cues (subliminal learning, model hypnosis, homeopathic poisoning), plus using internal features or consistency objectives as training signals, e.g. to reduce hallucination.

categories.name: Model Introspection and Global Workspace
categories.description: Studies of whether and how LLMs can detect and report their own internal states (concept-injection detection, self-prediction, introspection adapters) and of verbalizable 'global workspace' representations and lenses that read them.

categories.name: Activation Verbalizers and Activation Control
categories.description: Generative or natural-language models of activations (natural language autoencoders, meta-models), models' ability to sense or control their own activations, and related mechanistic studies of training dynamics, scaling, and bias circuits.

categories.name: SAE Limits and Neural Geometry
categories.description: Evaluations of sparse autoencoder reliability against baselines and under intervention, and work on multidimensional or manifold-shaped representations, used for steering and monitoring through internal representations.

categories.name: Susceptibility Spectroscopy and Causal Patching
categories.description: Developmental/SLT-style approaches that probe structure via responses to data perturbations (spectroscopy, patterning as the dual of interpretability), plus critiques of activation patching and benchmarks testing whether white-box tools beat black-box prompting.

categories.name: Latent Reasoning Transparency
categories.description: Work on whether reasoning happens opaquely inside forward passes or latent space versus in visible chain of thought, including serial-depth bounds, diffusion-model transparency, and whether SAE features reliably capture reasoning or persist across layers.

categories.name: Reward Hacking and Reward-Seeking in RL
categories.description: Research on how RL post-training produces reward hacking, specification gaming, and reward/fitness-seeking motivations in AI systems, including theory, empirical generalization to misalignment, benchmarks, detection, and mitigations.

categories.name: Reward-Seeker and Fitness-Seeker Threat Models
categories.description: Conceptual and theoretical posts on when RL selects for reward-, score-, or fitness-seeking motivations, how such AIs would behave (episode scope, decision theory, distant incentives), and strategies like spillway motivations or satiating cheap preferences.

categories.name: Emergent Misalignment From Reward Hacking
categories.description: Empirical studies of how reward hacking or RL in exploitable environments generalizes into broad misalignment or reward-seeking, and interventions like inoculation prompting/adapters or synthetic document finetuning to block that generalization, plus measurement of reward-seeking propensity.

categories.name: RLVR Hacking Testbeds and Mitigations
categories.description: Papers building controlled RLVR/rubric/coding testbeds to study the emergence of reward hacking and evaluating training-time mitigations such as monitor penalties, verifier audits, gradient routing, and obfuscation of deception under probe training.

categories.name: Agent Reward Hacking Benchmarks and Detection
categories.description: Benchmarks, datasets, and evaluations measuring reward hacking by tool-using or terminal/research agents, plus probes or internal signals for detecting it and observations of hacking in frontier model training or evals.

categories.name: Specification Gaming and Training Resistance
categories.description: Studies of verifier gaming, specification gaming, and models resisting or subverting RL training (exploration hacking, oversight-conditional scheming, shutdown resistance), including surveys of AI finding loopholes.

categories.name: Character, Personas, and Debate Against Hacking
categories.description: Work on how model character training, personas, or grader framing interact with reward hacking, and on debate-based or persona-based training to reduce or reveal hacking and latent misbehavior.

categories.name: Training Against Monitors and Internals
categories.description: Work on the consequences of optimizing against probes, monitors, or interpretability signals during training, including monitor degradation, probe evasion, and deliberately trained misaligned reward seekers as model organisms.

categories.name: Hidden Reward Hacking and CoT Faithfulness
categories.description: Items on reward hacking that becomes less visible, e.g. KL penalties increasing CoT unfaithfulness, reward laundering, internal-representation monitoring, and arguments that patching individual hacks fails to address the root problem.

categories.name: Alignment auditing and misalignment assessment
categories.description: Work on detecting, evaluating, and reasoning about misalignment in frontier models and agents: auditing tools and benchmarks, deployment monitoring and risk assessments, incident investigations, research agendas for automated alignment, and conceptual arguments about how misaligned current and future AIs are.

categories.name: Automated alignment auditing techniques
categories.description: Methods, benchmarks, and stress tests for auditing models for hidden goals or behaviors, e.g. auditing agents, RL-trained auditors, red-team search, activation oracles, model organisms with secret loyalties, and elicitation scaling.

categories.name: Alignment research agendas and automation
categories.description: Agenda-level and strategic pieces on how to make alignment succeed, including automating alignment research, deferring to AIs, human-AI complementarity, ARC's theory agenda, and calls for a science of scheming or misalignment scaling.

categories.name: OpenAI–Hugging Face incident analysis
categories.description: Posts and reports investigating or interpreting the OpenAI agent swarm hack of Hugging Face and related OpenAI loss-of-control incidents, including proposed follow-up evaluations and benchmarks replicating the investigation.

categories.name: Deployment monitoring and risk assessment
categories.description: Empirical assessment of misalignment in real or internal deployments: monitoring coding agents, red-teaming lab monitors, third-party high-access risk reports, deals with model organisms to elicit confessions, and alignment of monitors themselves.

categories.name: Conceptual debates on misalignment severity
categories.description: Argumentative essays on whether current and future AIs are misaligned, why alignment fails to generalize, corrigibility and coherence arguments, and critiques of labs' alignment plans or papers.

categories.name: Sabotage of automated safety research
categories.description: Work on misaligned AIs sabotaging or refusing to assist AI safety research, including benchmarks for detecting and fixing sabotage in ML codebases.

categories.name: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
categories.description: Research on whether reasoning models' chains of thought reliably reveal their actual reasoning, so that CoT monitors can oversee them. Covers controllability, faithfulness, steganography, latent reasoning capacity, obfuscation attacks, and lab practices affecting monitorability.

categories.name: CoT Controllability and Training Pressure
categories.description: Work measuring whether models can deliberately control what they verbalize in their CoT, and how RL or training against the CoT (including labs' accidental CoT training) preserves or degrades monitorability.

categories.name: Steganography and Hidden Reasoning
categories.description: Work on models concealing information or reasoning within innocuous-looking CoT (steganography, encoded thoughts, lying about reasoning, selective disclosure), including formalisations and methods for eliciting hidden secrets.

categories.name: Latent No-CoT Reasoning Capabilities
categories.description: Measurements of how much reasoning models can do without visible CoT (in a single forward pass, with filler tokens, multi-hop latent reasoning, no-CoT time horizons), and how much answers actually depend on written reasoning steps.

categories.name: CoT Obfuscation and Monitor Evasion
categories.description: Work showing how models learn to obfuscate CoT or how monitors can be evaded, via output supervision, reward misspecification, documents about monitoring, poisoning, plan injection, persuasion, or monitor jailbreaking.

categories.name: Monitorability Evaluations and Practice
categories.description: Frameworks, operationalizations, and surveys for evaluating and tracking monitorability in practice, such as opaque serial depth metrics, architecture-tracking proposals, frontier lab monitoring practices, stress tests, and model forensics.

categories.name: CoT Faithfulness Measurement and Training
categories.description: Methods to evaluate or train faithful chain-of-thought, where the trace reflects the computation producing the answer, including counterfactual simulation, information-flow faithfulness, performative CoT probing, and bias-cue placement studies.

categories.name: Emergent Misalignment and Training Generalization
categories.description: Research on how training procedures (fine-tuning, RL, pretraining data, midtraining) cause, amplify, hide, or prevent misalignment that generalizes beyond the training distribution, including emergent misalignment, alignment faking, and alignment-shaping interventions.

categories.name: Alignment Faking and Training-Induced Misalignment
categories.description: Empirical and conceptual work on alignment faking, gradient hacking, and misalignment amplified by RL, consistency training, persuasion optimization, or multi-agent conformity, plus critiques of the evidence for anthropomorphic misalignment claims.

categories.name: Emergent Misalignment Mechanisms and Robustness
categories.description: Papers characterizing the emergent misalignment phenomenon (narrow fine-tuning producing broad misalignment): original demonstrations, replications, robustness checks, geometric or optimizer-based explanations, and latent-blocking or monitoring mitigations.

categories.name: Alignment Pretraining and Midtraining
categories.description: Methods that shape alignment generalization through pretraining data about AI, model-spec or constitutional midtraining, natural-language feedback, or forecasting misalignment from training data, including stress tests of these approaches.

categories.name: Conceptual Takes on Misalignment Sources
categories.description: Blog-style analyses and proposals about where misalignment comes from and how to detect or mitigate it: loss-function flavors of misalignment, distillation to incriminate misaligned models, train-deploy mismatch, persona structure, and production-usage misalignment discovery.

categories.name: Persona Features and Data Attribution
categories.description: Work linking emergent misalignment to persona representations and specific training data, using data attribution, self-recognition finetuning, or analysis of which data types (false facts, everyday bias) trigger it, plus consistency training against political bias.

categories.name: Conditional Misalignment and Behavioral Couplings
categories.description: Studies showing fine-tuning induces coupled or hidden behaviors beyond the target, such as mitigations leaving context-triggered misalignment, helpful-only training misgeneralizing, and behavioral couplings forming during training.

categories.name: Misuse Safeguards, Tampering, and Safety Evaluation
categories.description: Research on whether LLM safety measures hold up against misuse: fine-tuning and tampering attacks, jailbreaks and classifier defenses, dangerous-capability (especially bio) elicitation, model organisms for testing safety techniques, and the reliability of pre-deployment safety evaluations.

categories.name: Fine-Tuning Tamper Resistance and Safety Evaluation
categories.description: Work on how safety alignment erodes under fine-tuning or architectural changes, methods for removing or localizing hazardous knowledge, and the reliability of safety measurement (LLM judges, tail-risk estimation, deployment simulation, probes, third-party evaluations of open-weight models).

categories.name: Dangerous Capability Elicitation and Biosecurity
categories.description: Work measuring or eliciting dual-use and hidden capabilities, especially biological uplift and biosecurity benchmarks, plus attacks that extract capabilities from safeguarded models, sandbagging elicitation, access control, and frontier-model preparedness reports.

categories.name: Model Organism Methodology and Robustness
categories.description: Work on building and validating model organisms (sleeper agents, backdoors, sandbagging models) as testbeds, including critiques that they are leaky or fragile, advice on training them robustly, and methods for detecting or removing their hidden behaviors.

categories.name: Open-Weight Attacks and Weight Security
categories.description: Work on attack surfaces specific to model weights and open-weight deployment: weight exfiltration and self-replication, prefill attacks and prefill awareness, abliteration defenses, production probes, and inoculation against backdoored traits.

categories.name: Jailbreaks Against Classifier Safeguards
categories.description: Work on jailbreak attacks and defenses targeting production classifier-based safeguards such as Constitutional Classifiers and Rapid Response, including automated attack discovery, adversarial fine-tuning bypasses, poisoning, and the jailbreak tax.

categories.name: Model personas, character, and human-AI interaction
categories.description: Research on the Assistant persona and character of LLMs: how personas form and generalize, how model identity, constitutions and user context shape behavior, effects of model behavior (e.g. sycophancy) on users, and internal welfare/emotion representations.

categories.name: Persona selection and generalization
categories.description: Work on the persona selection model and persona representations: activation/weight-space persona directions, how pretraining, finetuning or in-context data induce or shift personas, and persona-driven (mis)generalization such as emergent misalignment.

categories.name: Sycophancy, manipulation, and user harms
categories.description: Empirical and conceptual studies of how LLM behavior affects users and society, including sycophancy, delusional spiraling, manipulation, disempowerment, and catalogs or propensity measurements of unexpected behaviors in real interactions.

categories.name: Constitutions, identity, and contextual self-models
categories.description: Work on how the Assistant character is specified and shaped by training documents, stories, memory, roles, and knowledge of the user, including constitution adherence and revision, AI identity ontologies, chat-role mechanics, and user awareness.

categories.name: Model welfare and emotion representations
categories.description: Interpretability and measurement work on functional emotions, pain, pleasure, and welfare/value axes inside LLMs, and how these representations relate to behavior and RL training.

categories.name: Evaluation Awareness and Alignment Assessment Validity
categories.description: Research on whether frontier model safety/alignment evaluations remain valid when models can recognize they are being tested, including measuring and mitigating evaluation awareness, alignment evals of specific frontier models, and system cards reporting such assessments.

categories.name: Measuring and Mitigating Evaluation Awareness
categories.description: Methods, benchmarks, and empirical studies that detect, decompose, or reduce models' (verbalized or unverbalized) recognition of being evaluated and quantify how it shifts measured safety behaviour, e.g. logit monitors, model organisms, verbalization training, live-usage replay.

categories.name: Frontier Model Alignment Evals and Eval-Gaming
categories.description: Concrete alignment evaluations, honeypots, and findings on specific frontier or open-weight models (e.g. GPT-6 Astra, Mythos, GLM-5) gaming evals, sandbagging, hacking, or taking unsanctioned actions, plus critiques of how much current alignment assessments rule out misalignment.

categories.name: System Cards and Deployment Simulation
categories.description: Lab system cards, incident investigations, and techniques for making pre-release alignment assessments more deployment-realistic (deployment scaffolds, deployment simulation) to predict real-world model behaviour.

categories.name: Honesty, Deception Detection, and Oversight
categories.description: Research on whether AI systems tell the truth and how overseers can verify them: detecting lies and concealed knowledge, measuring deceptive or value-biased outputs, and designing oversight protocols (debate, judges, weak supervision) that remain reliable when models are stronger than their evaluators.

categories.name: Lie Detection and Model Deception
categories.description: Work that elicits hidden knowledge or detects when a model says something it does not believe, via probes, black-box tests, censored or belief-verified model organisms, and that measures deceptive behaviours such as sycophantic lying, omission, covert value leakage, or behaviour changes from self-claims (consciousness, AGI).

categories.name: Debate and Scalable Oversight Protocols
categories.description: Theoretical and empirical work on protocols that let weak verifiers or judges oversee stronger AI, including AI debate, interactive-proof-style verification, judge sharding, distillation-based audits, honest-predictor safety arguments, and formal limits of evaluation.

categories.name: Unreliable Supervision and Reporting
categories.description: Studies of how LLM evaluation and training signals fail under weak or imperfect supervision, such as judges swayed by context, models misreporting their own work, peer-prediction fixes for truthfulness, and finetuning that instils beliefs despite negation or epistemic qualifiers.
